newsitem.title: USA: Torotel sees Q4 charge for Defense issue.
newsitem.headline: Torotel sees Q4 charge for Defense issue.

text.p: Torotel Inc said Monday it expects to record a charge of about $414,000 in its fourth quarter relating to its failure to perform some tests on parts it sold to U.S. Department of Defense contractors.

The company, which makes switching power supplies and precision magnetic components, also said it entered into the defense department's Voluntary Discolosure Program, after discovering the testing error itself.

Torotel said voluntarily disclosing the failure to perform some required thermal shock testing as frequently as required and inaccurately certifying that the testing had been performed, would cut the amount of damages it would have to pay.
The issue involves Torotel's wholly-owned subsidiary, Torotel Products Inc.

Torotel also said it believes certain former officers may have been responsible for the misconduct and related test failures and is evaluating ways of recovering damages. The company said it suspended payment under a note payable to one former officer.
The company first reported the testing deficiencies in November.
The amount of the charge still is subject to fluctuation as further evidence is investigated, Torotel said.
Torotel shares closed unchanged at 1-1/16 Monday.
